cd "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-h-tegelbeckers-Library-CloudStorage-Nextcloud-cloud-ovgu-de-HannesTegelbeckers-PROF-INGPED-TECHED-Admin-Personal-Lehre-Tegelbeckers-Hannes/65105b6d-1d34-4828-b031-53372b15e15a/scratchpad/v3_work" && python3 -I - README.md <<'EOF'
import re,sys
t=open(sys.argv[1]).read().split('-->',1)[1]
t=re.sub(r'```.*?```','',t,flags=re.S)

    bad=set(notes)^steps
    print(('OK ' if not bad and len(notes)==len(set(notes)) else 'BAD'), s.splitlines()[0][:60], sorted(steps), notes)
print('PRÜFEN', t.count('PRÜFEN'))
EOF
grep -niE 'calibrat|troubleshoot|escalat|purpose limitation|value chain|visible in partner|lock-in' README.md
tool_input.description: Check slide count, notes per step, jargon

result:
I've rewritten the draft into a finished keynote in `README.md` and written the report to `improve_report.md`. It has 18 slides, inside the 14–18 range. I checked slide count, notes per step and the jargon list with searches; I couldn't run my Python check script or the lint tool because the command needed approval, so it has not been through the linter again.

**What changed:**
- **Less text on slides:** each reveal step shows about 5 short lines at most. Source details (Cedefop/ESCO, the UNESCO frameworks, the local AI server) moved into the speaker notes. Two small tables replace long bullet lists.
- **Plain English:** the jargon on the list is gone or explained once in one line: value chain, calibrate, troubleshoot, escalate, purpose limitation, lock-in, data sovereignty and OER (Open Educational Resources).
- **Nothing invented:** I removed "already visible in partner countries" and "true for every partner country". Both `PRÜFEN` markers are kept as `<!-- PRÜFEN: … -->`.
- **Title slide:** speaker name, university and event are now on the slide itself. I used "GIZ conference of the TVET and Labour Market community" because the brief gives no event name.
- **Speaker notes:** the draft had one note for a step that didn't exist (on the first poll), and in some places a list after a reveal marker wasn't actually hidden. Now each step has exactly one note, placed right after its block, written as 2–4 spoken sentences.
- **People instead of lists:** five illustrative people, each introduced with "Imagine …":
  - Amina, a job-seeker
  - a plumber in Nairobi, standing for informal work
  - Grace, a water technician
  - Joseph, an apprentice electrician
  - Sara, a vocational school teacher

  They come back in the take-aways.
- **Ending:** the second poll is now on its own "Your turn" slide (the one extra slide, 17 → 18). It ends with a concrete call to action: bring one real problem from your project to the conference discussions and name the person it is about.

**What I kept:** the five-part structure, the slide order, both polls, the "engine, drivers and roads" image, the text diagram of how labour market data flows, "If it is not in the data, it is not in the decision", the three take-aways and the closing line. I estimate about 55% of the draft survives.

**Before the talk:** two things are still marked for checking. One is whether the ILO figures on informal work are the latest. The other is whether to mention that this keynote itself was drafted with the Teaching Agent.
